newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai brokerages set up securities association.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai brokerages set up securities association.

text.p: Some 260 Shanghai brokerages and investment companies have set up a securities association to help improve their services and strengthen self-discipline, the Shanghai Securities News said on Sunday.
The Shanghai Securities Association on January 31 promulgated a charter requiring all brokers to conduct "open, fair and just" business, the newspaper said.
The charter said brokers must not directly hold or trade stocks or share warrants and must not abuse their powers for personal interest.
Brokers must not leak confidential information about their clients or trade without authority, and must not accept gifts from clients, the newspaper reported the charter as saying.
Those who violate the rules will be punished according to the charter, it said, and can have their trading licences revoked.
"The establishment of the association is aimed at improving the services of securities brokerages," the newspaper said. "It will also help self-discipline of brokerages."
The newspaper gave no further details.
